title: Theodicy
altTitle: Essais de Théodicée sur la bonté de Dieu, la liberté de l'homme et l'origine du mal
summary: The only book Leibniz published in his lifetime: a sustained answer to Pierre Bayle on the justice of God. A Preliminary Dissertation reconciles faith with reason; three parts of numbered articles defend divine goodness against the objections drawn from human freedom and the origin of evil; and a final Summary reduces the whole controversy to eight formal objections with answers. The most complete public statement of Leibniz's optimism — and the most complete test of it.
sourceNote: Seed text: Project Gutenberg eBook #17147 — the E. M. Huggard English translation of the Essais de Théodicée (1710), as distributed by Project Gutenberg in the US public domain. The Gutenberg edition also contains an editor's introduction (Austin Farrer) and two further appendix works; this edition includes only Leibniz's own text: the Original Preface, the Preliminary Dissertation, the three Parts (articles 1–417), and the Summary of the Controversy.
editorialNote: All 513 sections carry stable anchors (§Preface, §D1–§D87, §1–§417, §S1–§S8). Two transcription anomalies in the Gutenberg source were repaired editorially: article 237 (whose number was dropped in the source, beginning at the 'Second Syllogism') and article 328 (printed as a run-on inside the preceding paragraph) — both were re-anchored against the print edition's numbering. Page markers, emphasis underscores, and typographic noise were normalized during extraction. The French original (1710) awaits alignment before side-by-side reading can be enabled for this work.
